Where it began
2006
First Scopus-retrieved acknowledgment
Dönmez O., “The numerical simulation of perturbed accretion disk around the massive black hole”, International Journal of Modern Physics D (2006-07) — a black-hole accretion-disk simulation, crediting “TUBITAK/ULAKBIM super computers / Beowulf and T3E clusters”: the centre's original supercomputers, before the TR-Grid era even began.
Source-specific milestone: a different database can begin later because the record itself or its acknowledgment metadata is absent there; this is not evidence that TRUBA use began later.
Methodology
ⓘ Methodology & data — how these numbers are made
Publications crediting TRUBA / ULAKBİM computing in their funding acknowledgments. Journal quality uses SCImago SJR quartiles; citations are a snapshot at extraction, and the current year is still being indexed. Counts are a lower bound — only written acknowledgments can be found. Large-collaboration papers (ATLAS · CMS · Belle II) follow a different attribution basis and are reported separately on the WLCG page. Update schedule: the dashboard is refreshed monthly from Scopus and Web of Science (snapshot date in the header; next update: first week of August 2026); citation counts and recent-year totals change retrospectively as both databases continue indexing, so month-to-month movements in the current year are expected.
Conference papers: SJR ranks journals, so the 101 conference papers in this corpus are counted in the totals but excluded from the quality figures — Q1 share and citations per article are journal-article quantities. The UHeM dashboard does the same, so the two stay comparable.
This is a personal research project and is not an official TÜBİTAK or ULAKBİM website.
